diagram_math_checks.justification: The Example defines d=(v2-v1)/2 and m=(v1+v2)/2. Step 1.1 writes u=(a-b,a+b), so b is the output half-difference. The plotted map is R -> R, d -> b=S_{t lambda}(d), with t lambda>0 and one coordinate unit equal to t lambda on both axes.

diagram_math_checks.check: All three graph pieces and endpoint values
diagram_math_checks.justification: Fact F2 invokes the scalar soft-thresholding lemma; its F3 and the local soft-thresholding definition give b=d+t lambda for d<-t lambda, b=0 for |d|<=t lambda, and b=d-t lambda for d>t lambda. The plotted rays have slope one and meet the plateau at (-1,0),(1,0) in scaled units. The closed dots record the included threshold values b=0. There are no open endpoints or discontinuities.

Verification step 1.1 minimizes the a term at a=m; step 2.1 minimizes b at S_{t lambda}(d). Thus the plateau b=0 gives (m,m), the output mean is ((m-b)+(m+b))/2=m, and outside it |b|=|d|-t lambda with the same sign. This justifies every claim in the new caption.

The outer arrows extend the unbounded left and right affine branches; they are graph continuation arrows, not iteration or morphism arrows. Both threshold points meet the horizontal plateau continuously. This function plot is not a polygon or named-node cyclic graph; no closing edge is asserted. The existing numbered verification remains unchanged and independent of the figure.
